label: Meter
scope_note: Organization of beats into bars with recurring accents.

label: Simple meter
scope_note: Each beat divides into two.

label: 2/4 time
scope_note: Two beats per bar; marches, polka, cumbia.

label: 3/4 time
scope_note: Three beats per bar; waltz, mazurka, many folk ballads.

label: 4/4 time
scope_note: The default meter of nearly all popular music.

label: Compound meter
scope_note: Each beat divides into three.

label: 6/8 time
scope_note: Two triple-divided beats; jig, Irish ballads, slow doo-wop.

label: 9/8 time
scope_note: Three triple-divided beats, or aksak groupings (2+2+2+3).

label: 12/8 time
scope_note: Four triple-divided beats; slow blues, soul, rock and roll ballads.

label: Odd meter
scope_note: Bars whose beats don't group evenly.

label: 5/4 time
scope_note: Five beats (3+2 or 2+3).

label: 5/8 time
scope_note: Five eighth notes, grouped 2+3 or 3+2.

label: 7/8 time
scope_note: Seven eighth notes (2+2+3, 3+2+2…); prog rock, Balkan music.

label: 7/4 time
scope_note: Seven quarter notes per bar.

label: 11/8 time
scope_note: Eleven eighth notes; Balkan folk, progressive metal.

label: 13/8 time
scope_note: Thirteen eighth notes; prog rock and math rock.

label: Aksak rhythm
scope_note: Uneven groupings of 2s and 3s typical of Turkey and the Balkans.

label: Mixed meter
scope_note: Frequent alternation of different time signatures within a section.

label: Free meter
scope_note: Passages without a regular pulse, shaped by the phrase.

label: Hemiola
scope_note: Three duple beats laid over or alternating with two triple ones (metric 3:2).

label: Polymeter
scope_note: Simultaneous layers in different meters sharing a pulse.

label: Rhythmic feel
scope_note: How the pulse is subdivided and placed, beyond the time signature.

label: Straight feel
scope_note: Even subdivisions, no swing.

label: Swing
scope_note: Uneven (long-short) eighth notes built on a triplet.

label: Shuffle
scope_note: A steady, pronounced swing pattern; the basis of blues and boogie.

label: Triplet feel
scope_note: A pulse consistently subdivided into three.

label: Half-time feel
scope_note: The snare lands every other beat, so the music feels half as fast.

label: Double-time feel
scope_note: Percussion doubles the apparent speed of the pulse.

label: Laid-back feel
entry_terms: behind the beat; in the pocket
scope_note: Playing slightly behind the beat for a relaxed feel.

label: Driving feel
scope_note: Playing ahead of or insistently on the beat for urgency.

label: Rhythmic devices
scope_note: Techniques that alter or enrich the basic pattern.

label: Syncopation
scope_note: Accents on weak beats or between beats.

label: Anticipation
scope_note: A note or chord that arrives before the strong beat it was expected on.

label: Offbeat
scope_note: Systematic accenting of the weak parts of the beat.

label: Backbeat
scope_note: Snare accent on beats 2 and 4 of a 4/4 bar.

label: Polyrhythm
scope_note: Two or more conflicting subdivisions at once (3:2, 4:3…).

label: Three against two
scope_note: Three even notes against two in the same span.

label: Four against three
scope_note: Four notes against three in the same span.

label: Cross-rhythm
scope_note: Sustained polyrhythm as a structural basis, typical of West African music.

label: Clave
scope_note: Five-stroke guide pattern in Afro-Cuban music.

label: Son clave
scope_note: Son clave in its 3-2 and 2-3 orientations.

label: Rumba clave
scope_note: Variant with the third stroke delayed.

label: Bossa nova clave
scope_note: Brazilian clave variant used in bossa nova.

label: Tresillo
scope_note: 3+3+2 grouping of eighth notes, core of Afro-Latin rhythm and today's pop.

label: Habanera rhythm
scope_note: Tresillo with an added note on beat two.

label: Stop-time
scope_note: The band plays only isolated hits, leaving gaps for vocals or a solo.

label: Rhythmic displacement
scope_note: A motif repeated shifted against the beat.

label: Metric modulation
scope_note: Tempo change derived from a shared subdivision.

label: Anacrusis
scope_note: Notes before the first downbeat of a phrase.

label: Ensemble hits
scope_note: Accents played by the whole band together.

label: Tempo
scope_note: Speed of the pulse, in beats per minute.

label: Very slow tempo
scope_note: Below ~60 BPM.

label: Very fast tempo
scope_note: Above ~160 BPM.

label: Tempo change
scope_note: Tempo variation within the piece.

label: Accelerando
scope_note: Gradual speeding up.

label: Ritardando
scope_note: Gradual slowing down, typical of endings.

label: Rubato
scope_note: Expressive flexibility of tempo.

label: Fermata
scope_note: A note or rest held beyond its value.

label: Tempo switch
scope_note: Sudden jump to another tempo between sections.

label: Drum patterns
scope_note: Drum patterns that identify styles.

label: Basic rock beat
scope_note: Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, eighth-note hi-hats.

label: Four-on-the-floor
scope_note: Kick on every beat of a 4/4 bar; disco and house.

label: Stomp and clap beat
scope_note: Heavily accented alternating kick and handclap; glam and modern folk-pop.

label: Breakbeat
scope_note: Syncopated pattern taken from funk breaks, often sampled.

label: Amen break
scope_note: The break from "Amen, Brother" (The Winstons), foundation of jungle and drum and bass.

label: Chopped breaks
scope_note: Sampled breaks rearranged at high speed.

label: 2-step beat
scope_note: Syncopated pattern without a kick on every beat; UK garage.

label: Boom bap
scope_note: Dry, prominent sampled kick and snare; 90s hip hop.

label: Trap beat
scope_note: Sixteenth-note hi-hats with rolls, long 808, half-time snare.

label: Trap hi-hats
scope_note: Hi-hats with 32nd-note and triplet rolls.

label: Drill beat
scope_note: Displaced snare, triplet hi-hats and gliding 808.

label: Dembow
scope_note: Quarter-note kick with a tresillo snare (3+3+2); reggaeton.

label: One drop
scope_note: Kick and snare together only on beat three; roots reggae.

label: Steppers
scope_note: Quarter-note kick in reggae and dub.

label: Rockers beat
scope_note: Late-70s reggae pattern with busier kick and hi-hat.

label: D-beat
scope_note: Hardcore punk pattern derived from Discharge.

label: Skank beat
scope_note: Kick and snare alternating at high speed.

label: Blast beat
scope_note: Kick, snare and cymbals at maximum speed; grindcore and death/black metal.

label: Double bass drumming
scope_note: Kick played with two beaters in continuous sixteenths or bursts.

label: Gallop rhythm
scope_note: Eighth–two-sixteenths figure repeated on guitar or kick; classic heavy metal.

label: Motorik
scope_note: Hypnotic, steady 4/4 pulse; krautrock.

label: Train beat
scope_note: Continuous snare pattern imitating a train; country and rockabilly.

label: Purdie shuffle
scope_note: Half-time shuffle with ghost notes.

label: Second line
scope_note: New Orleans parade groove.

label: Bossa nova beat
scope_note: Cross-stick on the bossa clave with kick on 2.

label: Samba batucada
scope_note: Samba percussion with surdo, caixa and tamborim.

label: Baião rhythm
scope_note: Northeastern Brazilian rhythm with zabumba and triangle.

label: Cumbia rhythm
scope_note: Guacharaca or güira in eighths with kick in 2/4.

label: Tumbao
scope_note: Syncopated conga or bass pattern in salsa and son.

label: Afrobeat drumming
scope_note: Polyrhythmic drum pattern in the style of Tony Allen.

label: Jersey club beat
scope_note: Kick pattern in five-stroke bursts with bed-squeak samples.

label: Footwork beat
scope_note: Syncopated kick patterns at ~160 BPM.

label: Dancehall riddim
scope_note: Repeated rhythm track that different artists sing over.

label: Tamborzão
scope_note: Funk carioca percussion pattern derived from Miami bass.

label: Log drum groove
scope_note: Amapiano's percussive bass pattern.

label: Drum techniques
scope_note: Drumming performance techniques.

label: Ghost notes
scope_note: Very soft snare strokes between the main ones.

label: Drum fill
scope_note: Short drum phrase linking sections.

label: Drum roll
scope_note: Rapid, continuous succession of strokes.

label: Snare build-up
scope_note: Accelerating snare roll before a drop.

label: Flam
scope_note: Two near-simultaneous strokes, one a grace note.

label: Cross-stick
scope_note: Stroke with the stick resting across the rim.

label: Tribal toms
scope_note: Insistent patterns on the low toms.

label: Drum solo
scope_note: Showcase section for the drums.

label: Linear drumming
scope_note: No two strokes coincide; fluid funk and fusion patterns.

label: Brushes
scope_note: Playing with brushes; jazz and ballads.

label: Tonality
scope_note: Organization of pitches around a tonic.

label: Major key
scope_note: Major tonal center, generally bright in character.

label: Minor key
scope_note: Minor tonal center, generally dark in character.

label: Modality
scope_note: Harmony based on a mode rather than major/minor functions.

label: Atonality
scope_note: Absence of a tonal center.

label: Polytonality
scope_note: Two or more keys at once.

label: Microtonality
scope_note: Intervals smaller than a semitone.

label: Chords
scope_note: Chord types by construction.

label: Triad
scope_note: Three-note chord stacked in thirds.

label: Power chord
scope_note: Root and fifth with no third; the basis of rock and metal.

label: Seventh chord
scope_note: Triad with an added seventh.

label: Major seventh chord
scope_note: Soft-colored chord typical of jazz, soul and city pop.

label: Minor seventh chord
scope_note: Minor chord with a seventh; staple of R&B and neo soul.

label: Dominant seventh chord
scope_note: Tense chord that wants to resolve; everywhere in blues.

label: Half-diminished chord
scope_note: Diminished triad with a minor seventh.

label: Extended chords
scope_note: Chords with 9ths, 11ths or 13ths.

label: Suspended chord
scope_note: The third replaced by the second or fourth.

label: Added-tone chord
scope_note: Triad with an added note but no seventh.

label: Diminished chord
scope_note: Stacked minor thirds.

label: Augmented chord
scope_note: Stacked major thirds.

label: Altered chord
scope_note: Dominant with altered ninth or fifth.

label: Slash chord
scope_note: Chord with a note other than the root in the bass.

label: Quartal harmony
scope_note: Chords built in fourths; modal jazz.

label: Tone cluster
scope_note: Adjacent notes played together.

label: Neapolitan chord
scope_note: Major chord on the lowered second degree.

label: Harmonic devices
scope_note: Techniques of harmonic color and motion.

label: Modal mixture
scope_note: Chords borrowed from the parallel mode.

label: Secondary dominant
scope_note: Dominant of a degree other than the tonic.

label: Tritone substitution
scope_note: Replacing a dominant with the one a tritone away.

label: Chromatic mediant
scope_note: Chords a third apart with a chromatic change; typical of film scores.

label: Picardy third
scope_note: Minor-key piece ending on a major chord.

label: Tritone
scope_note: Three-whole-tone interval; unsettling sound much used in metal.

label: Dissonance
scope_note: Systematic use of tense, unresolved intervals.

label: Pedal point
scope_note: Sustained or repeated note under changing chords.

label: Reharmonization
scope_note: Changing the chords under a known melody.

label: Harmonic rhythm
scope_note: Rate at which chords change.

label: Jazz harmony
scope_note: Systematic use of seventh chords, extensions and substitutions.

label: Passing chord
scope_note: Brief chord connecting two structural chords.

label: Descending chromatic bass
scope_note: Bass descending by semitones under changing chords.

label: Line cliché
scope_note: An inner voice moves chromatically over a fixed chord.

label: Chord progressions
scope_note: Stock chord successions.

label: I–V–vi–IV progression
scope_note: The most-used pop progression since the 2000s.

label: I–vi–IV–V progression
scope_note: Progression of doo-wop and 50s pop.

label: ii–V–I
scope_note: Basic cadential cell of jazz.

label: Twelve-bar blues
scope_note: I-IV-V scheme over twelve bars.

label: Andalusian cadence
scope_note: Four-chord descent of flamenco and Spanish music.

label: Circle-of-fifths progression
scope_note: Roots descending by fifths.

label: Pachelbel progression
scope_note: Eight-chord progression of the Canon in D.

label: Royal road progression
scope_note: Signature progression of J-pop and anime.

label: i–VI–III–VII progression
scope_note: Minor progression of epic rock, EDM and trailers.

label: I–♭VII–IV progression
scope_note: Classic rock progression based on the Mixolydian mode.

label: Vamp
scope_note: Two chords alternating at length.

label: One-chord harmony
scope_note: Piece or section on a single chord.

label: Minor plagal cadence
scope_note: Minor subdominant resolving to a major tonic; very emotional.

label: Cadences
scope_note: Harmonic formulas that close a phrase.

label: Authentic cadence
scope_note: Dominant to tonic; conclusive close.

label: Plagal cadence
scope_note: Subdominant to tonic.

label: Half cadence
scope_note: Phrase ending on the dominant, left hanging.

label: Deceptive cadence
scope_note: The dominant resolves to an unexpected chord.

label: Backdoor cadence
scope_note: Arriving at the tonic from the flat seventh.

label: Modulation
scope_note: Change of tonal center within the piece.

label: Truck driver's modulation
scope_note: Key change up a half or whole step in the last chorus.

label: Pivot-chord modulation
scope_note: Key change via a chord common to both keys.

label: Direct modulation
scope_note: Key change without preparation.

label: Parallel key shift
scope_note: Switching between major and minor on the same tonic.

label: Scales
scope_note: Ordered pitch sets used as melodic material.

label: Major scale
scope_note: Diatonic major scale.

label: Natural minor scale
scope_note: Diatonic minor scale.

label: Harmonic minor scale
scope_note: Minor with a raised seventh; "neoclassical" sound.

label: Melodic minor scale
scope_note: Minor with raised sixth and seventh.

label: Pentatonic scale
scope_note: Five-note scales.

label: Major pentatonic
scope_note: Bright pentatonic; country, folk, East Asian music.

label: Minor pentatonic
scope_note: The basis of blues and rock solos.

label: Blues scale
scope_note: Minor pentatonic with an augmented fourth (the blue note).

label: Whole-tone scale
scope_note: Six notes a whole step apart; dreamlike effect.

label: Diminished scale
scope_note: Alternating whole and half steps; tension in jazz, metal and film scores.

label: Chromatic scale
scope_note: All twelve pitches by semitones.

label: Bebop scale
scope_note: Eight-note scale with a chromatic passing tone.

label: Altered scale
scope_note: Scale for altered dominants in jazz.

label: Phrygian dominant scale
scope_note: Phrygian with a major third; flamenco, klezmer and Middle Eastern music.

label: Double harmonic scale
scope_note: Scale with two augmented seconds.

label: Hungarian minor scale
scope_note: Harmonic minor with an augmented fourth.

label: Japanese scales
scope_note: Japanese pentatonics with semitones.

label: Modes
scope_note: Rotations of the diatonic scale, each with its own color.

label: Dorian mode
scope_note: Minor with a major sixth; funk, modal jazz, Celtic folk.

label: Phrygian mode
scope_note: Minor with a minor second; flamenco and metal.

label: Lydian mode
scope_note: Major with an augmented fourth; magical or floating sound, common in film scores.

label: Mixolydian mode
scope_note: Major with a minor seventh; classic rock and folk.

label: Locrian mode
scope_note: Mode with a diminished fifth; very unstable sound.

label: Modal and tuning systems
scope_note: Frameworks of particular traditions that go beyond a set of pitches: hierarchy of degrees, characteristic phrases, ornament, intonation or the tuning of an ensemble. Plain scales are under Scales.

label: Maqam
scope_note: Arabic and Turkish modal system with microtones.

label: Raga
scope_note: Melodic framework of Indian classical music.

label: Gamelan tuning systems
scope_note: General term; use Pelog or Slendro when the system is known.

label: Pelog
scope_note: Seven-tone gamelan tuning with unequal steps; pieces usually use five-tone subsets.

label: Slendro
scope_note: Five-tone gamelan tuning with nearly equal steps.

label: Melodic elements
scope_note: Recognizable melodic units.

label: Hook
scope_note: Short, catchy phrase designed to stick.

label: Riff
scope_note: Short repeated instrumental figure that carries the song.

label: Motif
scope_note: Smallest melodic or rhythmic idea that gets developed.

label: Leitmotif
scope_note: Motif tied to a character or idea that recurs.

label: Ostinato
scope_note: Persistently repeated figure.

label: Ground bass
scope_note: The repeated bass line itself; for the variation forms built on it use Passacaglia or Chaconne.

label: Countermelody
scope_note: Secondary line in dialogue with the main melody.

label: Topline
scope_note: Main sung melody over the track.

label: Arpeggio
scope_note: Chord notes played one after another.

label: Melodic sequence
scope_note: A motif repeated at other pitches.

label: Melodic devices
scope_note: Techniques of ornament and color in the line.

label: Chromaticism
scope_note: Use of out-of-scale notes by semitones.

label: Blue note
scope_note: Flattened, ambiguous third, fifth or seventh.

label: Ornamentation
scope_note: Decorative notes on the melody.

label: Trill
scope_note: Rapid alternation between two neighboring notes.

label: Mordent
scope_note: Quick ornament with a neighboring note.

label: Grace note
scope_note: Brief ornamental note before the main one.

label: Appoggiatura
scope_note: Leaning note on the beat that resolves by step; ornamental or harmonic.

label: Turn
scope_note: Ornament that circles the main note.

label: Glissando
scope_note: Slide through the pitches between two notes, continuous or as a rapid scale.

label: Portamento
scope_note: Expressive glide that connects one note to the next; on synthesizers often called glide.

label: Melisma
scope_note: The device; for a style of singing use Melismatic singing, for fast ornamental passages Vocal runs.

label: Syllabic setting
scope_note: One note per syllable.

label: Conjunct motion
scope_note: Melody moving by step.

label: Disjunct motion
scope_note: Melody with wide leaps.

label: Octave doubling
scope_note: Line doubled at the octave.

label: Improvisation
scope_note: Melodic creation in real time.

label: Modal improvisation
scope_note: Improvising over a mode with few chord changes.

label: Trading fours
scope_note: Soloists alternating every few bars.

label: Song sections
scope_note: Building blocks of a popular song. Many work as structure tags in prompts.

label: Intro
scope_note: Opening section before the first verse.

label: Verse
scope_note: Narrative section with changing lyrics.

label: Pre-chorus
scope_note: Section that builds tension before the chorus.

label: Chorus
scope_note: Central section repeated with the same lyrics.

label: Post-chorus
scope_note: Extra hook after the chorus.

label: Refrain
scope_note: Line repeated at the end of each verse.

label: Bridge
scope_note: Contrasting section, usually once, before the last chorus.

label: Interlude
scope_note: Instrumental or transitional section between parts.

label: Instrumental break
scope_note: Passage without vocals.

label: Solo section
scope_note: Showcase section for an instrument.

label: Guitar solo
scope_note: Electric or acoustic guitar solo.

label: Breakdown (metal)
scope_note: Slow, heavy section of syncopated muted chords.

label: Breakdown (EDM)
scope_note: Low-energy section without kick before the build.

label: Build-up
scope_note: Progressive rise in tension before the drop.

label: Drop
scope_note: Climax of an electronic track, where bass and kick come in.

label: Beat switch
scope_note: Complete change of beat mid-track; hip hop.

label: Hook (hip hop)
scope_note: The chorus of a rap track.

label: Skit
scope_note: Spoken piece or short scene on a hip hop record.

label: Spoken intro
scope_note: Recited opening before the music.

label: Final chorus
scope_note: Last chorus, often intensified or doubled.

label: Turnaround
scope_note: Chord passage leading back to the top of the form.

label: Tag ending
scope_note: Final repetition of the last line.

label: Outro
scope_note: Closing section.

label: Fade-out
scope_note: The song ends by gradually lowering the volume.

label: Cold ending
scope_note: Ending on a hit, no fade.

label: False ending
scope_note: Pause that fakes the ending before the music returns.

label: A cappella section
scope_note: Voices-only passage.

label: Dramatic pause
scope_note: Brief total silence for impact.

label: Song forms
scope_note: Overall organizational schemes.

label: Verse–chorus form
scope_note: Alternating verses and choruses with an optional bridge.

label: AABA form
scope_note: Form of the Tin Pan Alley standards.

label: Strophic form
scope_note: Same music for every verse.

label: Through-composed form
scope_note: No repeated sections.

label: Binary form
scope_note: Two contrasting sections.

label: Ternary form
scope_note: Statement, contrast and return.

label: EDM arrangement
scope_note: Intro–build–drop–breakdown–build–drop–outro.

label: Multi-part epic
scope_note: Long composition with linked movements; progressive rock.

label: Loop-based form
scope_note: Structure built by adding and removing layers over a loop.

label: Medley
scope_note: Chain of fragments from several songs.

label: Reprise
scope_note: Return of an earlier theme at the end of a record or work.

label: Segue
scope_note: Seamless transition from one piece to the next.

label: Compositional forms
scope_note: Forms of the art-music tradition, aligned with LCGFT.

label: Fugue
scope_note: Contrapuntal form based on imitation of a subject.

label: Canon
scope_note: Strict imitation of one voice by another after a delay.

label: Round
scope_note: Canon at the unison that repeats indefinitely.

label: Invention
scope_note: Short contrapuntal piece in two or three voices.

label: Sonata form
scope_note: Exposition, development and recapitulation of two themes.

label: Theme and variations
scope_note: A theme followed by successive transformations.

label: Passacaglia
scope_note: Variations over a repeated bass or progression.

label: Rondo
scope_note: Instrumental refrain alternating with episodes.

label: Toccata
scope_note: Virtuosic keyboard piece with fast figuration.

label: Prelude
scope_note: Introductory or short free-form piece.

label: Étude
scope_note: Piece focused on a technical difficulty.

label: Nocturne
scope_note: Lyrical, night-themed piano piece.

label: March
scope_note: Piece in 2/4 or 4/4 at a military pace.

label: Waltz
scope_note: Dance in 3/4 accented on beat one.

label: Minuet
scope_note: Courtly dance in 3/4.

label: Scherzo
scope_note: Fast, playful movement in 3/4.

label: Aria
scope_note: Lyrical solo vocal piece within a larger work.

label: Recitative
scope_note: Declaimed singing that follows speech rhythm.

label: Chorale
scope_note: Lutheran hymn harmonized in four parts.

label: Motet
scope_note: Sacred polyphonic choral composition.

label: Madrigal
scope_note: Secular polyphonic vocal composition of the Renaissance.

label: Mass
scope_note: Music for the Ordinary of the Mass.

label: Hymn
scope_note: Strophic song of praise.

label: Anthem
scope_note: Solemn, collective piece; by extension, a mass sing-along song.

label: Lullaby
scope_note: Soft song for sleep.

label: Lament
scope_note: Piece of mourning or grievance.

label: Serenade
scope_note: Amorous or light piece, originally performed at night.

label: Ballad
scope_note: Song that tells a story; in pop, a slow song.

label: Power ballad
scope_note: Ballad that builds to a finale with full-power guitars and drums.

label: Rhapsody
scope_note: Free, episodic piece.

label: Fantasia
scope_note: Free piece with an improvisatory character.

label: Cadenza
scope_note: Free, virtuosic solo passage.

label: Overture
scope_note: Introductory orchestral piece.

label: Suite
scope_note: Series of linked pieces or dances.

label: Concerto
scope_note: Work for soloist and orchestra.

label: Symphony
scope_note: Orchestral work in several movements.

label: Cantata
scope_note: Vocal work in several movements.

label: Oratorio
scope_note: Dramatic choral-orchestral work without staging.

label: Opera
scope_note: Staged drama sung throughout.

label: Jazz standard
scope_note: Repertoire tune used for improvisation.

label: Texture
scope_note: How simultaneous lines combine.

label: Monophony
scope_note: A single unaccompanied melodic line.

label: Homophony
scope_note: Main melody with chordal accompaniment.

label: Polyphony
scope_note: Several independent simultaneous lines.

label: Heterophony
scope_note: Simultaneous variants of the same melody.

label: Unison
scope_note: Several voices or instruments on the same pitch.

label: Sparse texture
scope_note: Few elements at a time, lots of space.

label: Dense texture
scope_note: Many simultaneous layers.

label: Counterpoint
scope_note: Combining independent lines under voice-leading rules.

label: Imitation
scope_note: One voice repeats another's material.

label: Voice leading
scope_note: How each voice moves between chords.

label: Hocket
scope_note: A melody split note by note between voices.

label: Accompaniment textures
scope_note: Typical accompaniment patterns.

label: Comping
scope_note: Rhythmic, irregular chords under a soloist.

label: Alberti bass
scope_note: Broken chord in low-high-middle-high order.

label: Harmonized lines
scope_note: Two instruments play the same line a third or sixth apart.

label: Drone
scope_note: Note or chord sustained throughout the piece.

label: Call and response
scope_note: Alternation between a solo phrase and a reply.

label: Antiphony
scope_note: Alternation between two choirs or groups.

label: Layering
scope_note: Elements entering progressively and stacking up.

label: Voice types
scope_note: Voice classification by range and ensemble.

label: Duet
scope_note: Two singers alternating or singing together.

label: Soprano
scope_note: Highest female voice.

label: Contralto
scope_note: Lowest female voice.

label: Countertenor
scope_note: Male voice in the alto range.

label: Tenor
scope_note: High male voice.

label: Baritone
scope_note: Middle male voice.

label: Bass voice
scope_note: Lowest male voice.

label: Choir
scope_note: Large vocal ensemble.

label: Gospel choir
scope_note: Gospel-style choir with handclaps and call and response.

label: Gang vocals
scope_note: Several voices shouting in unison; punk and hardcore.

label: Chant
scope_note: Collective singing recited on few notes.

label: Singing techniques
scope_note: Techniques of sung vocal production.

label: Chest voice
scope_note: Low, resonant register.

label: Head voice
scope_note: High, light register.

label: Falsetto
scope_note: High, airy register above the natural voice.

label: Belting
scope_note: Chest register pushed high with great power.

label: Mixed voice
scope_note: Blend of chest and head.

label: Vocal vibrato
scope_note: Periodic pitch oscillation.

label: Breathy vocals
scope_note: Delivery with lots of air.

label: Whisper
scope_note: Voice without vocal-fold vibration.

label: Vocal fry
scope_note: Crackly delivery in the lowest register.

label: Raspy vocals
scope_note: Light, rough distortion; rock and soul.

label: Twang
scope_note: Bright, nasal timbre; country.

label: Yodel
scope_note: Rapid jumps between chest voice and falsetto.

label: Vocal hiccup
scope_note: Clipped breaks in the voice; rockabilly.

label: Crooning
scope_note: Soft singing close to the microphone.

label: Operatic singing
scope_note: Classical technique projecting without a microphone.

label: Melismatic singing
scope_note: Style rich in melismas.

label: Vocal runs
scope_note: Fast passages of notes on one syllable; R&B and gospel.

label: Cante jondo
scope_note: Melismatic, raw flamenco singing.

label: Overtone singing
scope_note: One voice producing a note and its overtones at once.

label: Humming
scope_note: Singing with the mouth closed.

label: Whistling
scope_note: Whistled melody.

label: Vocalise
scope_note: Singing on vowels without text.

label: Scat singing
scope_note: Vocal improvisation with nonsense syllables; jazz.

label: Ululation
scope_note: High tongue trill, typical of North Africa and the Middle East.

label: Harsh vocals
scope_note: Distorted vocal techniques of metal and hardcore.

label: Growl
scope_note: Low guttural voice of death metal.

label: Scream
scope_note: Mid-to-high distorted scream.

label: Fry scream
scope_note: High scream based on vocal fry.

label: False chord scream
scope_note: Scream using the false vocal folds.

label: Shriek
scope_note: High shriek of black metal.

label: Pig squeal
scope_note: High, pig-like guttural of deathcore and slam.

label: Clean vocals
scope_note: Undistorted singing, in contrast to harsh vocals.

label: Shouted vocals
scope_note: Shouted, non-guttural voice; punk and hardcore.

label: Spoken and rapped vocals
scope_note: Non-sung vocal delivery.

label: Spoken word
scope_note: Spoken text over music.

label: Sprechgesang
scope_note: Technique halfway between speech and song.

label: Rap
scope_note: Rhythmic, rhymed delivery.

label: Flow
scope_note: Rhythmic pattern of a rap delivery.

label: Double-time rap
scope_note: Rap at double the apparent speed.

label: Triplet flow
scope_note: Rap in eighth-note triplets.

label: Melodic rap
scope_note: Rap with a melodic contour, often with autotune.

label: Mumble delivery
scope_note: Relaxed, loosely articulated diction.

label: Toasting
scope_note: Jamaican rhythmic chanting over riddims.

label: Beatboxing
scope_note: Percussion imitated with the mouth.

label: Vocal arrangement
scope_note: Arrangement of voices on the recording.

label: Vocal harmonies
scope_note: Several voices at different pitches.

label: Close harmony
scope_note: Tightly voiced parts; doo-wop, barbershop.

label: Double-tracked vocals
scope_note: The same vocal take recorded twice.

label: Ad-libs
scope_note: Spontaneous vocal interjections.

label: A cappella
scope_note: Voices without instrumental accompaniment.

label: Vocal call and response
scope_note: Soloist and choir alternating.

label: Guitar
scope_note: General term; use the narrower terms when the type of guitar is known.

label: Clean electric guitar
scope_note: Undistorted sound.

label: Electric sitar
scope_note: An electric guitar fitted to imitate the sitar, not a sitar.

label: Extended-range guitar
scope_note: Guitars with added low strings; modern metal.

label: Steel guitar
scope_note: Guitars played with a steel bar rather than by fretting; general term.

label: Lap steel guitar
scope_note: Played flat on the lap or on legs; for resonator instruments use Resonator guitar.

label: Resonator guitar
scope_note: Played lap-style or held like a guitar with a slide.

label: Baritone guitar
scope_note: Longer scale and lower tuning than a standard guitar; not the same as an extended-range guitar.

label: Cavaquinho
scope_note: Small four-string guitar of samba and choro.

label: Kora
scope_note: 21-string harp-lute of the Mandinka griots.

label: Cuatro
scope_note: The Venezuelan, Puerto Rican and related cuatros; for the Cuban tres use Tres.

label: Saz
scope_note: Long-necked lute of Turkey and Anatolia.

label: Đàn bầu
scope_note: One-string zither whose pitch is bent with a flexible rod.

label: Appalachian dulcimer
scope_note: Fretted plucked zither; not the hammered dulcimer.

label: Hammered dulcimer
scope_note: Struck with hammers, not plucked; listed here with the other zithers.

label: Tar (lute)
scope_note: The long-necked lute; the North African frame drum also called tar is a different instrument.

label: Fiddle
scope_note: Violin in folk, country and Celtic styles.

label: Rebab
scope_note: Name shared by several related bowed lutes; use with the tradition in view.

label: Siku
scope_note: Andean panpipes, often split between two players who alternate notes.

label: Didgeridoo
scope_note: Australian Aboriginal drone aerophone.

label: Electric grand piano
scope_note: A piano with strings and pickups; not an electric piano with tines or reeds.

label: Combo organ
scope_note: Transistor organ of the 1960s.

label: Diatonic button accordion
scope_note: Each button gives a different note on the push and on the pull.

label: String synthesizer
scope_note: Instrument, not the general sound of a string pad.

label: FM synthesis
scope_note: The method; for the instrument use Yamaha DX7.

label: Supersaw
scope_note: Stacked detuned saw waves; trance and EDM.

label: Acid bass
scope_note: TB-303 line with resonance and glides.

label: Reese bass
scope_note: Detuned saw bass; drum and bass.

label: Reverse bass
scope_note: Bass with a reversed envelope between kicks; hardstyle.

label: Wobble bass
scope_note: LFO-modulated bass; dubstep.

label: Hoover sound
scope_note: 90s rave synth sound.

label: Rave stab
scope_note: Short, aggressive synth chord.

label: Step sequencer
scope_note: Grid-programmed patterns that loop.

label: Roland TR-808
scope_note: Drum machine whose long kick doubles as bass.

label: Roland TR-909
scope_note: Drum machine of house and techno.

label: LinnDrum
scope_note: Drum machine of 80s pop.

label: Sound chip
scope_note: Sounds of vintage consoles and home computers.

label: Log drum
scope_note: Percussive bass sound of amapiano.

label: Frame drum
scope_note: General term; use the narrower terms for specific frame drums.

label: Mridangam
scope_note: Double-headed drum of Carnatic music.

label: Güira
scope_note: Metal scraper played with a wire brush; not the gourd güiro.

label: Dhol
scope_note: Double-headed drum from Punjab.

label: Gamelan
scope_note: Ensemble of metallophones and gongs from Java and Bali.

label: Balafon
scope_note: African xylophone with gourd resonators.

label: Anvil
scope_note: Struck as a percussion instrument.

label: Power trio
scope_note: Guitar, bass and drums.

label: Mariachi ensemble
scope_note: Trumpets, violins, guitarrón and vihuela.

label: Samba bateria
scope_note: Percussion section of a samba school.

label: Palm muting
scope_note: Strings damped with the palm for a dry, percussive sound.

label: Chugging
scope_note: Repeated low muted power chords.

label: Djent riffing
scope_note: Syncopated muted riffs on very low strings with a metallic attack.

label: Tremolo picking
scope_note: Very fast alternate picking on one note; black metal, surf.

label: Sweep picking
scope_note: Fast arpeggios with a sweeping pick stroke.

label: Tapping
scope_note: Notes sounded by the picking hand on the fretboard.

label: Legato (guitar)
scope_note: Slurred notes without picking.

label: Hammer-on
scope_note: A fretting finger strikes the string to sound a higher note without picking.

label: Pull-off
scope_note: A fretting finger pulls off the string to sound a lower note without picking.

label: String bending
scope_note: Stretching the string to raise the pitch.

label: Pinch harmonics
scope_note: High harmonics produced with the pick; metal.

label: Slide guitar
scope_note: Notes slid with a tube along the strings.

label: Fingerpicking
scope_note: Playing with the fingers.

label: Travis picking
scope_note: Alternating thumb bass with finger-played melody.

label: Rasgueado
scope_note: Fan-like strums of flamenco guitar.

label: Picado
scope_note: Fast scales plucked with alternating fingers.

label: Chicken picking
scope_note: Clucky, staccato country picking.

label: Funk guitar scratching
scope_note: Percussive strumming on muted strings.

label: Skank guitar
scope_note: Short offbeat chord; reggae and ska.

label: Jangle guitar
scope_note: Bright arpeggios of open chords; jangle pop.

label: Shred guitar
scope_note: Virtuosic high-speed solos.

label: Neoclassical shred
scope_note: Shred based on Baroque scales and arpeggios.

label: Guitar feedback
scope_note: Controlled amplifier feedback.

label: Drop tuning
scope_note: Tuning with the lowest string lowered.

label: Open tuning
scope_note: Tuning that forms a chord on open strings.

label: Chord melody
scope_note: Harmonized melody on a single guitar.

label: Slap bass
scope_note: Thumb slap and string pop.

label: Walking bass
scope_note: Quarter-note bass outlining the chords; jazz.

label: Octave bass
scope_note: Bass alternating octaves; disco.

label: Bass glides
scope_note: Pitch glides in the bass.

label: Stride piano
scope_note: Left hand alternating bass and chord; early jazz.

label: Boogie-woogie bass
scope_note: Left-hand blues figures in ostinato.

label: Montuno
scope_note: Syncopated, repeated piano figure in salsa.

label: Pizzicato
scope_note: Strings plucked with the fingers.

label: String tremolo
scope_note: Very fast bowed repetition.

label: Staccato strings
scope_note: The short articulation; for the bouncing bow stroke use Spiccato.

label: Spiccato
scope_note: Bow stroke that bounces off the string.

label: Col legno
scope_note: Striking with the wood of the bow.

label: Saxophone growl
scope_note: Saxophone with voice added; rough sound.

label: Brass stabs
scope_note: Short hits from the horn section.

label: Falls and doits
scope_note: Brass glissandos at the end of a note.

label: Scratching
scope_note: Moving the vinyl to create rhythms.

label: Recording aesthetic
scope_note: Overall character of the recorded sound.

label: Lo-fi
scope_note: Deliberately imperfect, saturated or muffled sound.

label: Polished production
scope_note: Clean, compressed, competitive sound.

label: Raw production
scope_note: Direct sound with little editing.

label: Live recording
scope_note: Concert or live-in-studio take.

label: Analog warmth
scope_note: The perceived quality; for the process use Tape saturation.

label: Wall of sound
scope_note: Dense layers with heavy reverb; Phil Spector, shoegaze.

label: Bass-heavy mix
scope_note: Bass dominates the mix.

label: Sub-bass
scope_note: Low frequencies below ~60 Hz, whatever instrument or synth produces them.

label: Dry mix
scope_note: Little reverb, close sound.

label: Field recording
scope_note: Environmental sounds recorded outside the studio.

label: Compression
scope_note: Reducing dynamic range.

label: Sidechain compression
scope_note: The signal ducks with each kick.

label: Spring reverb
scope_note: Metallic amplifier reverb; surf.

label: Gated reverb
scope_note: Abruptly cut-off reverb; 80s drums.

label: Shimmer reverb
scope_note: Reverb with an added upper octave.

label: Delay
scope_note: Repetitions of the signal.

label: Slapback echo
scope_note: Single short echo; rockabilly.

label: Dub echo
scope_note: Feedback delays manipulated live.

label: Chorus effect
scope_note: Slightly detuned doubling.

label: Tremolo effect
scope_note: Periodic volume variation.

label: Rotary speaker
scope_note: The effect of a rotating speaker cabinet, or its simulation; classic with the Hammond organ.

label: Distortion
scope_note: Clipping that adds harmonics.

label: Overdrive
scope_note: Mild tube saturation.

label: Tape saturation
scope_note: Soft compression and harmonic distortion from driving analog tape, or its emulation.

label: Fuzz
scope_note: Harsh, square-wave distortion.

label: Bitcrusher
scope_note: Digital resolution reduction.

label: Filter sweep
scope_note: Gradual opening or closing of a filter.

label: Resonant filter
scope_note: Filter with pronounced resonance; acid.

label: Wah-wah
scope_note: Foot-swept filter pedal.

label: Auto-Tune
scope_note: Audible pitch correction used as an effect.

label: Slowed and reverb
scope_note: Slowed-down version with reverb; or the chopped and screwed technique.

label: Reverse
scope_note: Recording played backwards.

label: Stutter edit
scope_note: Choppy repetitions of a fragment.

label: Tape stop
scope_note: Simulated tape slowdown to a halt.

label: Sampling
scope_note: Reusing recorded fragments.

label: Loop
scope_note: Fragment repeated cyclically.

label: Vocal chops
scope_note: Chopped vocal fragments used as an instrument.

label: Sample flip
scope_note: Creative transformation of a recognizable sample.

label: Sound design
scope_note: Non-musical sound elements with a structural role.

label: Riser
scope_note: Rising sound that builds tension.

label: Downlifter
scope_note: Falling sound after a climax.

label: Impact
scope_note: Low hit at the start of a section.

label: Braam
scope_note: Distorted low brass from trailers.

label: Sub drop
scope_note: Pitch drop in the sub-bass.

label: Era aesthetic
scope_note: Production traits associated with a decade.

label: Dynamics
scope_note: Management of volume and intensity.

label: Crescendo
scope_note: Gradual increase in intensity.

label: Sforzando
scope_note: Sudden, strong accent.

label: Dynamic contrast
scope_note: Alternating soft and explosive sections.

label: Slow build
scope_note: Intensity that grows throughout the piece.

label: Articulation
scope_note: How notes are attacked and connected.

label: Staccato
scope_note: Short, separated notes.

label: Legato
scope_note: Notes connected without a break.

label: Lyrical devices
scope_note: Lyric-writing devices.

label: Rhyme scheme
scope_note: Distribution of rhymes (AABB, ABAB…).

label: Internal rhyme
scope_note: Rhymes within the same line.

label: Multisyllabic rhyme
scope_note: Chained multi-syllable rhymes; rap.

label: Storytelling
scope_note: The lyrics tell a story with characters.

label: Punchline
scope_note: Witty closing line; rap.

label: Title drop
scope_note: The title appears in the hook.

label: Vocables
scope_note: Meaningless sung syllables.

label: Code-switching
scope_note: Switching languages within the lyrics.

label: Protest lyrics
scope_note: Social or political lyrics.

label: Confessional lyrics
scope_note: Intimate first-person lyrics.

label: Instrumental
scope_note: Piece without vocals.

label: Mood
scope_note: Affective descriptors. Not technical devices, but music-generation prompts rely on them heavily.

label: Anthemic
scope_note: Made to be sung by a crowd.
